note: Adjudicated accidental and house-orthography variants, and one chant-book omission. The Missal and the digital witness agree on the substantive text; the Liber Usualis prints no et at w005, recorded below. The Mass of the Sunday after the Ascension reprints this Offertory on p. 347 of the same Benziger edition, identical in letters, accents and punctuation to p. 346.

adjudicated.ruling: The chant book marks the singing accent on this word (Déus); the approved Benziger printing prints Deus unaccented, and the edition follows the Missal.
The approved Benziger printing's spelling is retained under the house orthography. The witness reading is the same word in another editorial spelling.
The chant book prints the same word with consonantal j (jubilatióne); the approved Benziger printing's iubilatióne is retained under the house orthography.

The approved Benziger printing (p. 346) and the digital witness print et before Dóminus; the chant book has no et here (p. 849). The edition follows the Missal and records the omission without adopting it.
The chant book marks the singing accent on this word (vóce); the approved Benziger printing prints voce unaccented, and the edition follows the Missal.
The chant book prints the digraph ae and marks the singing accent (túbae); the approved Benziger printing prints tubæ with the ligature, and the edition follows the Missal.
The approved Benziger printing's spelling is retained under the house orthography. The witness reading is the same word in another editorial spelling.
